messages.author: f065beb80677617c
messages.subject: Habitat-specific density estimates (birds)
parts:
Hello everyone

Sorry to have to post to the list, I was hoping to find an answer on a discussion or in one of the R vignettes, but couldn't. I have something of a problem because my analysis plans have changed since I collected data, meaning my study design is less than optimal!

I have a study consisting of:
  • 25 1 km^2 squares ("sites") in variably heterogenous habitats. i.e. some are uniform forest/pasture, others are mixes of two or more habitat types.
  • Within each site I have 12 "points", visited once each, where I conducted point counts with distance sampling for birds. 
  • At each point I know the coverage of different habitats, again this is variably heterogenous.
  • Using the count data for each bird species at each point and the variable proportions of different habitats at each point, I would like to estimate the mean density in each habitat type (eventually for each species, but one to begin with would be a start!).
My plan was to use a modified version of the models used by Royle et al. 2004, with proportion of each habitat type as a covariate within the Poisson model (presumably arcsin transformed?!) and site as a random effect in the model. 

However... a) I wasn't sure whether this was actually a good idea b) I couldn't find details of the specific functions Royle et al. used c) a later paper (Sillett et al.  2012) explicitly states that their update of Royle et al.'s model "assumes that density is constant within each plot", which is the opposite of what I want to assume. Is it possible to get around this?

Sorry the verbosity and vagueness, any help or pointers would be gratefully received.

David

Royle, J. A., Dawson, D. K., & Bates, S. (2004). MODELING ABUNDANCE EFFECTS IN DISTANCE SAMPLING. Ecology, 85(6), 1591–1597. doi:10.1890/03-3127

Sillett, T. S., CHANDLER, R. B., Royle, J. A., KÉRY, M., & Morrison, S. A. (2012). Hierarchical distance-sampling models to estimate population size and habitat-specific abundance of an island endemic. Ecological Applications, 22(7), 1997–2006.

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Habitat-specific density estimates (birds)
parts:
hi David,

 unmarked will not handle random effects. For this, I suggest using WinBUGS (see the Kery 2010 and Kery and Schaub 2011 books for many examples and templates, although not about distance sampling).

 If you don't pursue the random effects then I agree you could use "% habitat type x" as a set of covariates in the mean:
 log(lambda(point)) = beta0 + beta1*log(x1) + beta2*log(x2) + ....
 which I think is pretty standard for modeling compositional data. Or maybe using some other transformation as you suggest.

 Ideally you would parameterize the Poisson mean like this:

 lambda(point) = sum_{k} lambda(k)*xk

where the xk sum to 1.  That is, express the expected density as an area-weighted sum of the constituent pieces. This would be easy to do in WinBUGS but not in unmarked.

regards
andy
